questions.question: A solid sphere of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is divided into two unequal parts. The smaller part having mass $M/8$ is converted into a sphere of radius $r$ and the larger part is converted into a circular disc of thickness $t$ and radius $2R$. If $I_1$ is moment of inertia of a sphere having radius $r$ about an axis through its centre and $I_2$ is the moment of inertia of a disc about its diameter, the ratio of their moment of inertia $I_2/I_1 = $ _____.
questions.solution:
Let the mass of the original solid sphere be $M$ and its radius be $R$.

Mass of the smaller sphere, $m_1 = \dfrac{M}{8}$.
Since the material remains the same, the density is constant. The volume is directly proportional to the mass.
$\dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \dfrac{1}{8} \left(\dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3\right) \Rightarrow r^3 = \dfrac{R^3}{8} \Rightarrow r = \dfrac{R}{2}$

Moment of inertia of the smaller sphere about an axis through its centre is:
$I_1 = \dfrac{2}{5} m_1 r^2 = \dfrac{2}{5} \left(\dfrac{M}{8}\right) \left(\dfrac{R}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{2}{5} \times \dfrac{M}{8} \times \dfrac{R^2}{4} = \dfrac{M R^2}{80}$

Mass of the larger part (which is converted into a disc) is:
$m_2 = M - \dfrac{M}{8} = \dfrac{7M}{8}$

The radius of the disc is given as $2R$. The moment of inertia of a disc about its diameter is:
$I_2 = \dfrac{1}{4} m_2 (\text{radius})^2 = \dfrac{1}{4} \left(\dfrac{7M}{8}\right) (2R)^2 = \dfrac{1}{4} \times \dfrac{7M}{8} \times 4R^2 = \dfrac{7M R^2}{8}$

The ratio of their moments of inertia is:
$\dfrac{I_2}{I_1} = \dfrac{\dfrac{7M R^2}{8}}{\dfrac{M R^2}{80}} = \dfrac{7}{8} \times 80 = 70$

Answer: $70$

questions.question: A circular disc has radius $R_{1}$ and thickness $T_{1}$. Another circular disc made of the same material has radius $R_{2}$ and thickness $T_{2}$. If the moment of inertia of both discs are same and $\frac{R_{1}}{R_{2}}=2$ then $\frac{T_{1}}{T_{2}}=\frac{1}{\alpha}$. The value of $\alpha$ is $\_\_\_\_$.
questions.solution:
For a circular disc made of material with density $\rho$, moment of inertia is $I = \frac{1}{2}MR^2 = \frac{1}{2}\rho \pi R^2 T \cdot R^2 = \frac{1}{2}\rho \pi R^4 T$.
For disc 1: $I_1 = \frac{1}{2}\rho \pi R_1^4 T_1$
For disc 2: $I_2 = \frac{1}{2}\rho \pi R_2^4 T_2$
Given $I_1 = I_2$:
$R_1^4 T_1 = R_2^4 T_2$
With $\frac{R_1}{R_2} = 2$:
$(2R_2)^4 T_1 = R_2^4 T_2$
$16 R_2^4 T_1 = R_2^4 T_2$
$\frac{T_1}{T_2} = \frac{1}{16}$
Therefore $\alpha = 16$.

Axis through midpoints of top and bottom sides (along y-direction).

Moment of inertia of the rod about axis $AB$ passing through one of its ends:
$I_{\text{rod}} = \dfrac{ML^2}{3} = \dfrac{40 \times (3)^2}{3} = \dfrac{40 \times 9}{3} = 120\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2$

Moment of inertia of the solid sphere about the same axis $AB$, using the parallel axis theorem $I = I_{\text{cm}} + md^2$:
Mass $m = 10\text{ kg}$, radius $R$, distance from the centre of the sphere to axis $AB$ is $d = 3\text{ m}$.

$I_{\text{sphere}} = \dfrac{2}{5}mR^2 + md^2 = \dfrac{2}{5}(10)R^2 + 10(3)^2 = 4R^2 + 90$

Equating the two moments of inertia:
$120 = 4R^2 + 90$
$4R^2 = 30$
$R^2 = \dfrac{15}{2}$
$R = \sqrt{\dfrac{15}{2}}$

Comparing with $R = \sqrt{\dfrac{\alpha}{2}}$:
$\alpha = 15$

Hence, $\alpha = 15$.

questions.question: Suppose there is a uniform circular disc of mass $M \mathrm{~kg}$ and radius $r \mathrm{~m}$ shown in figure. The shaded regions are cut out from the disc. The moment of inertia of the remainder about the axis $A$ of the disc is given by $\frac{x}{256} M r^{2}$. The value of $x$ is $\_\_\_\_$.
questions.solution:
The moment of inertia of the complete disc about axis A is
$I_{disc} = \frac{1}{2}Mr^2 = \frac{128Mr^2}{256}$.
Each removed circular region has radius $r/4$ and mass $m_i = M/(r^2/16r^2) = M/16$.
For each removed disc at distance $3r/4$ from axis A, using the parallel axis theorem:
$I_{removed} = \frac{1}{2}m_i(r/4)^2 + m_i(3r/4)^2 = \frac{Mr^2}{512} + \frac{9Mr^2}{256} = \frac{19Mr^2}{512}$.
For two removed discs:
$I_{2removed} = \frac{38Mr^2}{512} = \frac{19Mr^2}{256}$.
Therefore:
$I_{remainder} = \frac{128Mr^2}{256} - \frac{19Mr^2}{256} = \frac{109Mr^2}{256}$, so $x = 109$.

questions.question: A solid sphere of radius 10 cm is rotating about an axis which is at a distance 15 cm from its centre. The radius of gyration about this axis is $\sqrt{n} \mathrm{~cm}$. The value of $n$ is
questions.solution:
Using the parallel axis theorem for radius of gyration:
$k^2 = k_{cm}^2 + d^2$ where $k_{cm}$ is the radius of gyration about the center of mass and $d$ is the distance from the center.
For a solid sphere:
$I_{center} = \frac{2}{5}MR^2$, so $k_{cm}^2 = \frac{2}{5}R^2$
With $R = 10$ cm and $d = 15$ cm:
$k^2 = \frac{2}{5}(10)^2 + (15)^2 = 40 + 225 = 265$
Since $k = \sqrt{n}$, we have $n = 265$.

questions.question: A fly wheel is accelerated uniformly from rest and rotates through $5rad$ in the first second. The angle rotated by the fly wheel in the next second, will be :
questions.solution:
Here the angular acceleration is constant, so we have,

$\theta = \omegat + \dfrac{1}{2}\alpha{t}^{2}$.

When flywheel is rotated from rest in the first second, then ${θ}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}\alpha\left(1\right)2 = 5rad$

$⇒ \alpha = 10rad{s}^{- 2}$

The angle turned by flywheel in the next second is ${θ}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\alpha\left(2\right)2 = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(10\right)\left(4\right) = 20rad{s}^{- 2}$

Thus, the angle turned during next second is $\theta = 20 - 5 = 15rad$

questions.question: A thin solid disk of 1 kg is rotating along its diameter axis at the speed of 1800 rpm. By applying an external torque of $25 \pi \mathrm{Nm}$ for 40 s, the speed increases to 2100 rpm. The diameter of the disk is ________ m.
questions.solution:
Given, $\mathrm{m}=1 \mathrm{~kg}$
$\begin{aligned}
& \omega_{\mathrm{i}}=1800 \mathrm{rpm}=1800 \times \frac{2 \pi}{60}=60 \pi \frac{\mathrm{rad}}{\mathrm{sec}} \\ & \omega_{\mathrm{f}}=2100 \mathrm{rpm}=2100 \times \frac{2 \pi}{60}=70 \pi \frac{\mathrm{rad}}{\mathrm{sec}} \\ & \tau_{e x t}=25 \pi \mathrm{Nm} \\ & \mathrm{t}=40 \mathrm{sec}
\end{aligned}$
Using equation of motion
$\begin{aligned}
& \omega_{\mathrm{f}}=\omega_{\mathrm{i}}+\alpha \mathrm{t} \\ & 70 \pi=60 \pi+\alpha(40) \\ & \alpha=\frac{\pi}{4} \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{sec}^2
\end{aligned}$
Also, $\tau=\mathrm{I} \alpha$
$\tau=\frac{\mathrm{mR}^2}{4} \alpha$
$\begin{aligned}
& 25 \pi=\frac{1 \times \mathrm{R}^2}{4} \times \frac{\pi}{4} \\ & \mathrm{R}=20 \mathrm{~m}
\end{aligned}$
Hence, diameter of disk $=2 \mathrm{R}=2 \times 20=40 \mathrm{~m}$

questions.question: A solid sphere of radius $4$ cm and mass $5$ kg is rotating (rotation axis is passing through the centre of the sphere) with an angular velocity of $1200$ rpm. It is brought to rest in $10$ s by applying a constant torque. The torque applied and the number of rotations it made before it comes to rest are _______ and _______ respectively.
questions.solution:
Initial angular velocity $\omega_0 = 1200 \text{ rpm} = \dfrac{1200 \times 2\pi}{60} = 40\pi \text{ rad/s}$

Final angular velocity $\omega = 0$

Time $t = 10 \text{ s}$

Angular acceleration $\alpha = \dfrac{\omega - \omega_0}{t} = \dfrac{0 - 40\pi}{10} = -4\pi \text{ rad/s}^2$

Moment of inertia of the solid sphere $I = \dfrac{2}{5}MR^2 = \dfrac{2}{5} \times 5 \times (0.04)^2 = 0.0032 \text{ kg m}^2$

Torque $\tau = I|\alpha| = 0.0032 \times 4\pi = 0.0128\pi \text{ Nm}$

Angle rotated $\theta = \dfrac{\omega_0 + \omega}{2}t = \dfrac{40\pi + 0}{2} \times 10 = 200\pi \text{ rad}$

Number of rotations $N = \dfrac{\theta}{2\pi} = \dfrac{200\pi}{2\pi} = 100$

Answer: $0.0128\pi$ Nm, $100$

Two blocks of mass of $M$ and $m$ are attached to two ends of a light string passing over the pulley, which is hinged to rotate freely in vertical plane about its center. The magnitudes of the acceleration experienced by the blocks is $\_\_\_\_$ (assume no slipping of string on pulley).
questions.question: The pulley shown in figure is made using a thin rim and two rods of length equal to diameter of the rim. The rim and each rod have a mass of $M$. Two blocks of mass of $M$ and $m$ are attached to two ends of a light string passing over the pulley, which is hinged to rotate freely in vertical plane about its center. The magnitudes of the acceleration experienced by the blocks is $\_\_\_\_$ (assume no slipping of string on pulley).
questions.solution:
The pulley consists of a rim (mass $M$) and two rods (each mass $M$) forming a diameter structure.
The moment of inertia is: $I = I_{rim} + I_{rods} = MR^2 + 2 \times \frac{MR^2}{3} = \frac{5MR^2}{3}$.
For the Atwood pulley system, applying Newton's second law:
Mass $m$ (upward): $T_1 = m(g-a)$
Mass $M$ (downward): $T_2 = M(g+a)$
Pulley rotation: $T_2 R - T_1 R = I\alpha = \frac{5MR^2}{3} \cdot \frac{a}{R}$
Thus: $T_2 - T_1 = \frac{5Ma}{3}$
Substituting: $M(g+a) - m(g-a) = \frac{5Ma}{3}$
$(M-m)g + (M+m)a = \frac{5Ma}{3}$
$(M-m)g = a\left(\frac{5M}{3} - M - m\right) = a\left(\frac{2M}{3} - m\right)$
$a = \frac{(M-m)g}{\frac{2M-3m}{3}} = \frac{3(M-m)g}{2M+3m}$, which is option (2).

questions.q: Two masses $m$ and 2 m are connected by a light string going over a pulley (disc) of mass 30 m with radius $r=0.1 \mathrm{~m}$. The pulley is mounted in a vertical plane and it is free to rotate about its axis. The 2 m mass is released from rest and its speed when it has descended through a height of 3.6 m is $\_\_\_\_$ $\mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$. (Assume string does not slip and $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}$)
questions.question: Two masses $m$ and 2 m are connected by a light string going over a pulley (disc) of mass 30 m with radius $r=0.1 \mathrm{~m}$. The pulley is mounted in a vertical plane and it is free to rotate about its axis. The 2 m mass is released from rest and its speed when it has descended through a height of 3.6 m is $\_\_\_\_$ $\mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$. (Assume string does not slip and $\mathrm{g}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}$)
questions.solution:
Let the speed of the masses be $v$ and the angular velocity of the pulley be $\omega = v/r$ since the string does not slip.
The pulley is a disc of mass $M = 30m$ and radius $r$. Its moment of inertia is $I = \frac{1}{2}Mr^2 = \frac{1}{2}(30m)r^2 = 15mr^2$.
Using the principle of conservation of mechanical energy, the loss in potential energy of the system equals the gain in kinetic energy.
When the mass $2m$ descends by $h = 3.6$ m, the mass $m$ ascends by $h = 3.6$ m.
Loss in potential energy $\Delta U = (2m)gh - (m)gh = mgh$.
Gain in kinetic energy $\Delta K = \frac{1}{2}(2m)v^2 + \frac{1}{2}(m)v^2 + \frac{1}{2}I\omega^2$.
Substituting $I$ and $\omega$: $\Delta K = \frac{3}{2}mv^2 + \frac{1}{2}(15mr^2)(\frac{v}{r})^2 = \frac{3}{2}mv^2 + \frac{15}{2}mv^2 = 9mv^2$.
Equating $\Delta U = \Delta K$: $mgh = 9mv^2$.
$v^2 = \frac{gh}{9}$.
Given $g = 10$ m/s$^2$ and $h = 3.6$ m:
$v^2 = \frac{10 \times 3.6}{9} = \frac{36}{9} = 4$.
$v = \sqrt{4} = 2$ m/s.

questions.solution:
The rod is pivoted at a distance $\frac{L}{3}$ from one end. The centre of mass is at a distance $\frac{L}{6}$ from the pivot.
Using energy conservation:
$mg\frac{\ell}{6} = \frac{1}{2}I\omega^2$
Moment of inertia about the pivot (using parallel axis theorem):
$I = \frac{m\ell^2}{12} + m\left(\frac{\ell}{6}\right)^2 = \frac{m\ell^2}{12} + \frac{m\ell^2}{36} = \frac{m\ell^2}{9}$
$mg\frac{\ell}{6} = \frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{m\ell^2}{9} \cdot \omega^2$
$\omega^2 = \frac{9g}{6 \cdot \frac{\ell}{2}} = \frac{3g}{\ell}$
$\omega = \sqrt{\frac{3g}{\ell}}$

A. The linear momentum $\vec{p} = \left(2\hat{i} + 1.5\hat{j}\right)$ kg·m/s.
B. The force acting on the object $\vec{F} = \left(2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}\right)$ N.
C. The angular momentum of the object about its origin $\vec{L} = 15\hat{k}$ J·s.
D. The torque acting on the object about its origin $\vec{\tau} = 20\hat{k}$ N·m.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Given the position vector $\vec{r} = 10t^2\hat{i} + 5t^3\hat{j}$

Velocity $\vec{v} = \dfrac{d\vec{r}}{dt} = 20t\hat{i} + 15t^2\hat{j}$

Acceleration $\vec{a} = \dfrac{d\vec{v}}{dt} = 20\hat{i} + 30t\hat{j}$

At $t = 1$ s:
$\vec{r} = 10\hat{i} + 5\hat{j}$ m
$\vec{v} = 20\hat{i} + 15\hat{j}$ m/s
$\vec{a} = 20\hat{i} + 30\hat{j}$ m/s$^2$

Linear momentum $\vec{p} = m\vec{v} = 0.1(20\hat{i} + 15\hat{j}) = 2\hat{i} + 1.5\hat{j}$ kg$\cdot$m/s (Statement A is correct)

Force $\vec{F} = m\vec{a} = 0.1(20\hat{i} + 30\hat{j}) = 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}$ N (Statement B is correct)

Angular momentum $\vec{L} = \vec{r} \times \vec{p} = (10\hat{i} + 5\hat{j}) \times (2\hat{i} + 1.5\hat{j}) = (10 \times 1.5 - 5 \times 2)\hat{k} = 5\hat{k}$ J$\cdot$s (Statement C is incorrect)

Torque $\vec{\tau} = \vec{r} \times \vec{F} = (10\hat{i} + 5\hat{j}) \times (2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j}) = (10 \times 3 - 5 \times 2)\hat{k} = 20\hat{k}$ N$\cdot$m (Statement D is correct)

Therefore, statements A, B, and D are correct.

Answer: A, B and D only

If we take the wheel as a ring then its moment of inertia will be, $I = M{r}^{2}$.

Using mechanical energy conservation,

$Mgh - mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}M{v}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}I{ω}^{2} ⇒ 12gh - 3gh = \dfrac{1}{2}3{v}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}12{v}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}12{r}^{2}\dfrac{v2}{r2}$

$⇒ 9gh = \dfrac{15{v}^{2} + 12{v}^{2}}{2}$

$⇒ v = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}gh} = \dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{\dfrac{8}{3}gh}$

Therefore, $x = \dfrac{8}{3} ≃ 3$

questions.q: A solid sphere ($A$) of mass $5m$ and a spherical shell ($B$) of mass $m$, both having same radius, are placed on a rough surface. When a force of same magnitude is applied tangentially at the highest points of $A$ and $B$, they start rolling without slipping with an acceleration of $a_A$ and $a_B$, respectively. The ratio of $a_A$ and $a_B$ is __________.
questions.question: A solid sphere ($A$) of mass $5m$ and a spherical shell ($B$) of mass $m$, both having same radius, are placed on a rough surface. When a force of same magnitude is applied tangentially at the highest points of $A$ and $B$, they start rolling without slipping with an acceleration of $a_A$ and $a_B$, respectively. The ratio of $a_A$ and $a_B$ is __________.
questions.solution:
For a body of mass $M$ and radius $R$ rolling without slipping under a force $F$ applied tangentially at the highest point, the torque about the point of contact with the ground is $\tau = F(2R)$.

The moment of inertia about the point of contact is $I = I_{cm} + MR^2$.

Using $\tau = I\alpha$ and the rolling without slipping condition $a = \alpha R$, we get:

$F(2R) = (I_{cm} + MR^2) \dfrac{a}{R} \Rightarrow a = \dfrac{2FR^2}{I_{cm} + MR^2}$

For the solid sphere $A$ of mass $5m$:

$I_{cm,A} = \dfrac{2}{5}(5m)R^2 = 2mR^2$

$a_A = \dfrac{2FR^2}{2mR^2 + 5mR^2} = \dfrac{2F}{7m}$

For the spherical shell $B$ of mass $m$:

$I_{cm,B} = \dfrac{2}{3}mR^2$

$a_B = \dfrac{2FR^2}{\dfrac{2}{3}mR^2 + mR^2} = \dfrac{2F}{\dfrac{5}{3}m} = \dfrac{6F}{5m}$

The ratio of their accelerations is:

$\dfrac{a_A}{a_B} = \dfrac{\dfrac{2F}{7m}}{\dfrac{6F}{5m}} = \dfrac{2}{7} \times \dfrac{5}{6} = \dfrac{5}{21}$

Answer: $5 : 21$

At time $t=0$ the cylinder has a translational velocity $v_0=49$ m/s, perpendicular to its axis and a rotational velocity $v_0/4R$ about the centre. The time taken by the cylinder to start rolling is ________ seconds. (coefficient of kinetic friction $\mu_K=0.25$ and $g=9.8$ m/s$^2$)
questions.question: A solid cylinder having radius $R$ and length $L$ is slipping on a rough horizontal plane. At time $t=0$ the cylinder has a translational velocity $v_0=49$ m/s, perpendicular to its axis and a rotational velocity $v_0/4R$ about the centre. The time taken by the cylinder to start rolling is ________ seconds. (coefficient of kinetic friction $\mu_K=0.25$ and $g=9.8$ m/s$^2$)
questions.solution:
Initial translational velocity, $v_0 = 49$ m/s.

Initial angular velocity, $\omega_0 = \dfrac{v_0}{4R}$.

Velocity of the lowest point of the cylinder is $v_{bottom} = v_0 - \omega_0 R = v_0 - \dfrac{v_0}{4} = \dfrac{3v_0}{4} > 0$.

Since the lowest point is slipping forward, kinetic friction $f_k = \mu_k m g$ acts in the backward direction.

Translational acceleration, $a = -\dfrac{f_k}{m} = -\mu_k g$.

Angular acceleration, $\alpha = \dfrac{f_k R}{I} = \dfrac{\mu_k m g R}{\dfrac{1}{2} m R^2} = \dfrac{2\mu_k g}{R}$.

At time $t$, the translational velocity is $v = v_0 - \mu_k g t$.

The angular velocity is $\omega = \omega_0 + \alpha t = \dfrac{v_0}{4R} + \dfrac{2\mu_k g}{R} t$.

For pure rolling to start, $v = \omega R$.

$v_0 - \mu_k g t = \left( \dfrac{v_0}{4R} + \dfrac{2\mu_k g}{R} t \right) R$

$v_0 - \mu_k g t = \dfrac{v_0}{4} + 2\mu_k g t$

$3\mu_k g t = \dfrac{3v_0}{4}$

$t = \dfrac{v_0}{4\mu_k g}$

Substituting the given values $v_0 = 49$ m/s, $\mu_k = 0.25$, and $g = 9.8$ m/s$^2$:

$t = \dfrac{49}{4 \times 0.25 \times 9.8} = \dfrac{49}{9.8} = 5$ s.

Answer: $5$
